title: A MORPHOGRAPHIC IDEONOMIC ATLAS OF THE “<DIRECTLY + INDIRECTLY> <INTUITED, CALCULATED, AND SCALED> OVERALL MUTUAL ‘ANALOGOUSNESS’” OF “THIRTY-TWO KEY GENERA OF FORMS” — Atlas No. II
notes:
N=32
FORMS & Morphology

* * * CAVEATS AND EXPLANATIONS * * *

This ideonomic morphographic atlas represents an EXPERIMENTAL HYBRID, because weights of the indicated ‘analogousness’ values were ONLY in ONE-THIRD-PART derived from a DIRECT form of Triadic Method nMDS scaling of the scalees, whereas they were in TWO-THIRDS-PART the product of the INDIRECT, and still uncertain, SCALEE-SCALOR INVERSION technique. More precisely, the tabulated dyadic ‘Form-Form’ values are the sums of a triplicate form of scaling, involving 40 DIRECT scalors (former Scaling Dyads) and TWO SETS of 32 (hence 64) INDIRECT scalors (80% of the former LEFT and RIGHT ANTIMONADS within those 40 Scaling Dyads); or a maximum potential ‘analogousness’ value of 104. In short, the ‘analogousness’ values are 38% direct, and 62% indirect. Such triplicate valuation was only possible because of the great itemic redundancy between the original <Scalee, Left-Antimonadic-Scalor, and Right-Antimonadic-Scalor> Sets. Although the two 40-antimonad sets were compositionally identical, only 32 of the corresponding ‘Forms’ had ever actually been scaled directly.

The effect of this triplication, or summation of three independent valuations, should, IN PRINCIPLE, be to greatly enhance: the <accuracy, validity, depth, and complexity> of the “analogical” <absolute and relative> <weights and orderings>, of the picture they hopefully will paint of the <nature, properties, typology, taxology, laws, spaces, and possibilities> of these Form Genera (and of the universe of form in general), and of any practical uses which may be made of them.

But it will be immediately evident, upon inspection of these thirty-two scales, that the scales are only rough and allow, indeed require, many corrections and refinements. What they most successfully provide is a clear indication that this sort of thing is in fact feasible, and that, properly carried out, it could have real value to the scientific community and be a useful addition to the general methods and means of scientific research.

The original Scaling Question was: “Which form genus is {THE SCALEE} most analogous to?”

The small atlas was simply produced as a side-product of Ideonomy Project EXERCISE #41,595-B, conducted 1991 November 30, in the ideonomic division “FORMS (Morphology)”.
